description:
## Context

QuickHeadlines on FreeBSD crashes after 1-2 days of uptime with
excessive memory growth (observed: 9GB VIRT after 1.5h; 4.3GB RSS
after 22h; full system crash after 1-2 days). The in-progress
investigation `quickhea-alz` confirmed EventBroadcaster was leaking
client references; that fix landed in the previous commit (c1a067d0).

This epic enumerates the remaining suspected leak vectors based on a
code review against the principles in planning/architecture.md
(resource management, "Memory efficiency - does this avoid
unnecessary allocations or leaks?", bounded data structures, no
global mutable state between modules).

## Suspected leak vectors (by file/area)

1. **favicon_storage.cr @client_pool** — Hash(String, HTTP::Client)
   keyed by host. Each unique feed host adds an HTTP::Client with
   its own socket pool / TLS context. Grows unbounded as unique
   hosts are seen. `close_pooled_clients` is only called by
   `MemoryManagerActor.clear_system_caches` on `Aggressive` /
   `Emergency` priority — never on the normal path. **This is the
   single most likely remaining leak after quickhea-alz** because
   it follows the same "unbounded global Hash" pattern that caused
   the EventBroadcaster crash.

2. **fetcher/feed_fetcher_concurrent.cr lines 42, 133, 135** —
   per-feed inner fibers are spawned via tracked_spawn and the
   `result_channel = Channel(FeedData?).new(1)` allocation is not
   GC-prompted; if the inner fiber holds it past the timeout (via
   closure capture of `feed`, `previous_feed_data`, `index`), it
   lingers. With 100+ feeds every 30 min, this is 100+ inner
   fibers + 100+ channels retained per cycle, plus the outer
   fibers. The `feed` reference inside the closure retains the
   parsed feed config including any TLS state.

3. **infrastructure/actor.cr lines 257, 301** — every `def_call`
   allocates a fresh `Channel(String).new(1)`. If the caller
   raises between `send_message` and `receive`, or under a 30s
   timeout, the channel + Call{Method} struct linger. With high
   call rates (RateLimiter, MemoryManagerActor.get_rss_mb on every
   API request, SocketManager stats, etc.) this is hundreds of
   short-lived channels/minute. The RateLimiter design comment
   already calls this out: "the leak (per-call def_call
   allocations) is the priority issue".

4. **websocket/socket_manager.cr writer fiber line 342** —
   spawned per connection; exits only when `outgoing.close` is
   called by `handle_unregister_connection` /
   `handle_connection_closed` / `handle_shutdown_all` /
   `handle_cleanup_dead`. Risk: a half-closed TCP socket that the
   runtime does not notice as `closed?` keeps the writer fiber
   spinning and holding `conn` + any pending broadcast payloads.
   The janitor runs only on demand, not periodically.

5. **fetcher/refresh_supervisor.cr `run_timed_refresh` lines
   249-288** — On the `timeout(outer_timeout)` branch, the worker
   fiber is signalled with `cancel_ch.send(nil)` but **not
   joined**. The worker continues running until `refresh_all`
   notices the cancel and raises `CancelError`, retaining
   `config_snapshot` + any partial `fetched_map` for the duration.
   This is a per-cycle leak that compounds across cycles.

6. **utils/string_pool.cr StringIntern** — MAX_POOL_SIZE=10000,
   eviction via `keys.first(MAX_POOL_SIZE // 2)` returns a new
   Array of references to the keys being deleted; the keys array
   itself is a transient leak. Interned values are not deduped
   across the value side (only the key side), so eviction is
   mostly fine for the pool itself. Add this to the audit to
   confirm retention policy is correct.

7. **fetcher/refresh_supervisor.cr `run_initial_refresh` line
   207** — `initial_cancel_ch` is set but signal is only sent
   from `run_first_cycle` if `QuickHeadlines.shutting_down?` is
   true at the *end* of the first sleep. If the process is killed
   or restarted mid-sleep, the initial refresh fiber retains
   `config_for_initial` and the @cache, @db_service references
   until it naturally completes.

8. **app_state_service.cr @memory_history** — capped at 500, OK.
9. **app_state_service.cr track_memory_usage** — comment is
   misleading ("only track every 10 updates to reduce overhead")
   but semantics are fine; not a leak. Note for cleanup.
10. **event_broadcaster.cr @@client_history** — capped at 1000,
    OK (post-quickhea-alz fix).
11. **rate_limiter.cr @@allowed_cache** — bounded at 256, OK.
12. **favicon_cache.cr** — bounded at 200, OK.

## Goals

- Identify the dominant leak(s) with measurements, not guesses.
- Cap all unbounded data structures in the long-lived paths
  (connections, fibers, actor channels, HTTP clients).
- Add forced GC + per-cycle heap snapshots so future leaks are
  diagnosable in 10 min, not 22 h.
- Keep QuickHeadlines stable on FreeBSD for >=7 days under
  nominal load with RSS under 1 GB.

## Acceptance

- Heap snapshots before/after each fix, RSS growth over 24 h
  < 100 MB on the same config as the FreeBSD production jail.
- All child tasks closed; bw sync clean.
- No new lints (ameba) and spec suite green.

## Sequencing

```mermaid
graph LR
  1[Add heap snapshot + RSS delta instrument] --> 2[Audit unbounded data structures]
  2 --> 3[Cap FaviconActor client pool]
  2 --> 4[Cap SocketManager writer fiber retention]
  2 --> 5[Cap actor reply channel lifetime]
  2 --> 6[Add periodic forced full GC backstop]
  3 --> 7[Long-running FreeBSD soak test 48h]
  4 --> 7
  5 --> 7
  6 --> 7
  1 --> 7
```
title: Memory leak investigation & fixes (1-2 day FreeBSD crash)
